findings.title: Public methods dereference a null item list without validation
findings.evidence: The subtotal loop iterates directly over the caller-provided list, and totalWithTax passes its items argument straight through to subtotal with no null guard. A null list now causes an immediate NullPointerException instead of a controlled validation error.
findings.recommendation: Validate public inputs at method entry, for example reject null items with IllegalArgumentException or treat null as an empty list consistently in both subtotal and totalWithTax.

findings.title: Null taxRate causes a reachable NullPointerException in totalWithTax
findings.evidence: The method multiplies subtotal by taxRate without checking for null, so any caller passing a null tax rate will crash at runtime.
findings.recommendation: Add an explicit null check for taxRate at the start of totalWithTax and fail with a clear IllegalArgumentException, or define and implement a default such as zero tax.

findings.title: Negative tax rates are accepted and can produce invalid negative invoice totals
findings.evidence: There is validation for unitPrice and quantity, but totalWithTax applies any taxRate directly. With a taxRate less than -1, the computed tax exceeds the subtotal in magnitude and the returned invoice total becomes negative, which is an invalid billing result in normal supported use.
findings.recommendation: Validate taxRate to the supported domain, typically taxRate >= 0, and reject out-of-range values before computing totals.
